summary: Prevent native and TileLang contact scatter from writing shared static velocity slots.
regressions: Native Coulomb and twist contact warmstart/solve/cached tests preserve signed-zero static velocity bits while updating dynamic bodies.
The write predicate retains angular-only and linear-only responsive endpoints.
Sixteen native color cases share one static endpoint across 1, 33, 65 and 129 constraints; C and Metal execution compare dynamic results and preserve static words exactly.
Color validation rejects both directions of static-read/dynamic-write aliasing as well as dynamic write/write aliasing.
differences: This is a Rust reference bug fix, applied to ordinary, fused and warmstart scatter in the shared Coulomb/twist implementation. A zero impulse does not make concurrent non-atomic writes valid.
TileLang mirrors the zero inverse mass/inertia guard. The existing non-colored replay and supplied-manifold TGS contracts retain their narrower disjoint-slot precondition.
Fused native entry points use the guard but their GPU synchronization and the TileLang fused optimization remain outside current execution coverage.
No tolerance is loosened. Ascend source lowering does not establish device execution or memory-model correctness.
